findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
The loop recalculates available unknown time from unchanged `intervals` for every folded task. When two long tasks in one story have overlapping folded ranges, both can reassign the same seconds, making the story's unknown time negative and its working and waiting totals too large. Even one folded task can misclassify time when another task works during part of its folded range: the code assigns the remaining unknown time to working first, without knowing when the folded task actually worked. The new story proof uses only one part, so it does not exercise either overlap.
findings.title: Story breakdown miscounts overlapping folded task time

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Test
The `story-part` proof reads the board but asserts only the story's working, waiting and unknown fields; its total-time assertion applies to the task row, not the story row. A regression that makes the board report an incorrect `story["total_seconds"]` while leaving those category fields intact would pass this named proof. The Done-when line explicitly requires the board to show the total time.

why: A long item's pull request time record grows toward GitHub's 64 KB body limit, and Forge trims older time detail from about round 16
